name: BuildMap
mission: Make software construction visible: show what each piece does, what is actually connected, what is still missing, and how every verified piece moves the system toward the intended outcome.

components.name: Intent recovery
components.purpose: Start from available intent evidence — README, docs, manifest, or an owner description — without blocking the map.
components.contributes: Keeps the build focused on what the project is actually trying to accomplish.

components.name: Repository scanner
components.purpose: Inventory source, discover bounded relationships, assess evidence and declared outcome walkthroughs, and show gaps without assuming end-to-end behavior.
components.contributes: Turns source code into the living set of puzzle pieces.

components.name: Live map server
components.purpose: Serve current maps and actionable gaps, export an offline HTML snapshot, or guide explicitly requested local project descriptions, piece grouping and walkthrough plans.
components.contributes: Makes progress visible while the software is being built instead of after the fact.

components.name: Interactive visualizer
components.purpose: Inspect pieces, source wiring, evidence, and declared outcome walkthroughs with recorded inputs/outputs; mini-visuals are illustrations, not runtime traces.
components.contributes: Lets a human spot gaps, understand progress, and see why a file matters at a glance.

components.name: Verification evidence
components.purpose: Check source/evidence semantics, outcome plans and example freshness, Git inventory, export safety, CLI/HTTP behavior, and client logic with a DOM harness; browser layout still needs observation.
components.contributes: Prevents BuildMap from confusing 'exists on disk' with 'actually proven to work.'

outcomes.name: Understand the current build
outcomes.goal: Open a repository map, understand the purpose of its pieces, and inspect the gaps and evidence behind the build.

steps.label: Agree on the goal
steps.expected: A declared or attributed goal; unknown intent stays visible.
steps.explanation: We want BuildMap to help you see what has been built, how the pieces fit together, and what still needs work. This step reads the project's stated goal so the map stays focused on that purpose.

steps.label: Check what's built
steps.expected: A snapshot separating implementation, source connections, evidence, outcomes, and gaps.
steps.explanation: BuildMap looks through the project files and builds a picture of the pieces, their connections, and the evidence behind them. It makes missing parts and unproved behavior visible.

steps.label: Make the results available
steps.expected: The current snapshot is available through the local HTTP API or a standalone export.
steps.explanation: BuildMap delivers that picture to the viewer, or packages it into a file you can open and share.

steps.label: Review what works
steps.expected: A person can locate a piece or outcome and understand its files, purpose, evidence, examples, and next gap.
steps.explanation: You select a piece or walkthrough step to see what it does, why it matters, and what still needs attention. This is where you can check whether the build is serving the goal.

finishedProduct.experience: You open your project and see a clear visual map of its pieces, files, connections and goals. Select a piece to understand its job in plain English, or select a goal to follow its steps beside the map. The wider free walkthrough shows readable steps and recorded examples, with the first unfinished point clearly visible.
finishedProduct.behavior: Help beginner-to-intermediate builders understand how a complete application fits together, see what has actually been demonstrated, and keep coding-agent work focused on the intended result. The complete map, current goal walkthroughs and basic focused task briefs are free. Missing work and unsupported claims stay visible so progress is grounded in evidence. BuildMap Guide adds a first source-bound JavaScript function-reading preview. Guide also prepares user-reviewed tasks with acceptance criteria and exact file scope, and compares later local snapshots with the agreed baseline. Criteria still require actual checks; Guide tasks can be explicitly saved on the device and exported/imported with their original baseline. Billing remains unconfigured.
